reason: The rejection holds on all four ideas. I checked each citation. (A) The 73/13,284 GT match for readmitted final nodes is right (round7 report, round2 v_plancheck_pc2-13, 56-clip exp60 lab). The '1,337 of 121,777' figure is the exp56/K1 dummy count (CONTEXT l.1515), not the lab pool, which is a small mix-up. The '+-1e-4' size is too low: 13,284 flagged nodes are ~1.4% of the ~0.9M lab final nodes, so removing them all could move the node-count term by up to ~+0.001, minus the edges of the ~73 matched nodes. But the rejection is stronger than the finding says, because the idea has already been tested on the LB. Leaf prune on x138 removed 95% readmitted nodes (CONTEXT l.1511-1516, l.2033): lab lp30 +0.00083, P36 delta 0 on the LB, closed. Readmit knobs are R4 by name (l.1650), and the LB anchors show readmit at -0.001 (l.1884). So a DeepCenter readmit veto is leaf prune in disguise, a closed line, and R4's +0.002 is out of reach. (B) R2 allows 'only the #35 configuration, no ladders' (l.1643-1646). The ensemble p is less extreme than fold p (99th pct 0.83 vs 0.90; CONTEXT 24 Sep 00:15Z), so a fold-p arm does not replay the kernel. Confirmed. (C) The V2 checklist (l.2041) says never tick P36 and tick #34 only when no eligible non-copy file exists. Confirmed. (D) z shift was closed by round-8 R8-RC-A (refuted: embryo-dependent bias of 44b6 +0.15 vs 6bba +0.45 um, honest size +0.0003..0.0005). Confirmed. On feasibility: none of the four could pass an honest gate, a dummy, a new OK and the R3/R4 adoption rule before R8 (27 Sep 12:00Z). Finals stay #37 + #38.
